sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3124/2022 That on 26.05.2022 at about 5.30 p.m, when the Petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA23EQ6050 towards Velankani circle to BHL and when he reached near Paradisi Biriyani hotel, Velankani road, Electronic city, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753 came in a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle from opposite direction.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner fell down and had sustained grievous injuries to both legs and other parts of the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Narayana Clinic and after first aid he was shifted to Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
He had spent total Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Security Guard and was earning 30,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3124/2022 he is permanently disabled and he lost his future employment.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40 EA 5753 by its rider.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.

6. The Respondent No.1 in its detailed Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3124/2022 treatment.
Further it contended that the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA 5753 is not at all involved in the accident.
Further it contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner and it has prayed to Chandrashekar Tammanna Yadravi vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83719113/
2 dismiss the Petition against it.
7.

sentences.text: On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 26.05.2022 at about 5.30 p.m. on Velankani Road,
near Paradise Biriyani hotel, Phase1, Electronic City, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA 5753 by its rider?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3124/2022 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award?
8. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P11.
Further, he examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.12 and 13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.

9. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753 by its rider.
11. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753 by its rider.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Charge sheet, Discharge summary, Medical bills, Prescriptions, Xrays, Aadhaar card, Spot mahazar, Wound certificate and DL.
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3124/2022 13.

Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the Mahalakshmi who is the wife of the Petitioner, the Electronic City Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.9 is the true copies of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.

Ex.P.10 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner issued by Dr. Gopalappa H.M of M.S. Ramaiah hospital which shows the following injuries:
1) Swelling and tenderness over right knee.
Abrasions 1X1cm present.
ROM restricted and painful at right knee 2) Tenderness and swelling over left foot and ankle 14.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, both injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.3 is the True copy of the Charge sheet SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3124/2022 which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Electronic City Traffic Police Station against the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.

Further, the Petitioner has examined Doctor by name Dr. B. Ramesh as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.12 and 13.
17.
P.W.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.1 has examined its Legal Manager by name Naveena S. as RW.1.
But, nothing could be elicited to disprove the contention of the PW.1.
Chargesheet is the material document which shows that the I.O has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the motorcycle.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent riding of the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3124/2022 offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA23EQ 6050 by its rider and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
18. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 35 years.
Further, in the Aadhaar card and DL i.e., Ex.P8 & 11, date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 29.01.1986.
The accident took place on 26.05.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 37 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
20. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as Security Guard and was earning 30,000/ per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
22.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P10 issued by the Medical Officer of the M.S. Ramaiah hospital,
Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1) Swelling and tenderness over right knee.
Abrasions 1X1cm present.
ROM restricted and painful at right knee 2) Tenderness and swelling over left foot and ankle SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3124/2022
As per the opinion of the Doctor, both injuries are grievous in nature.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
25. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken inpatient treatment at M.S. Ramaiah Hospital.

Upon going through Ex.P.4  Discharge summary of M.S. Ramaiah SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3124/2022 Hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 27.05.2022 to 13.06.2022.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 19 days.
26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 46,500/ under this head (@ 15,500/ per month ).

sentences.text:
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3124/2022 compensation of 9,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards attendants charges,
9,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 27,000/ under this head.
V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
28. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced total 47 medical bills and hospital bills total amounting to 20,349/ which are marked at Ex.P5.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.20,400/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,400/ under this head.

SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3124/2022 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS /
COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
29. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

30. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. B. Ramesh as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at M.S. Ramaiah hospital.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 19%.
PW.2 got marked OPD card and Xray at Ex.P12 and 13.
In the crossexamination PW.2 admitted that he did not treat the Petitioner.
He further admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united and he also admitted that in the matter of fracture, the age of the injured is also an important point.

He further admitted that the problems in the movement of the SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3124/2022 Petitioner will be cured in Physiotherapy treatment and if a person had undergone continuous physiotherapy treatment there will be reduce in his problems and also in the Stability component.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
31. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of 15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 2,23,200/ (15,500/ x 12 = 1,86,000/
, 1,86,000/x 15 x 8/100 = 2,23,200/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 2,23,200/ under this head.

32. To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  40,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  30,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  46,500/ up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  27,000/ and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses Rs.20,400/
6. Loss of Future Income 2,23,200/ Total 3,87,100/
33.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 3,87,100/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

34. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3124/2022 and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA40EA5753.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
35. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3124/2022  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 3,87,100/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
